candidates.title: [RFC]: SM90 DeepGEMM MegaMoE for DeepSeek V4
candidates.snippet: ## Motivation  vLLM's current DeepGEMM MegaMoE backend is SM100-only (its support check hard-requires device capability 100), and all SM100 formats rely on Blackwell features (TMEM, UTCCP, MX datatypes). Hopper (SM90) has no megakernel path.  DeepSeek V4 ships two routed-expert precisions:  - `expert_dtype="fp4"` (Flash): MXFP4, served by the existing SM100 path. - `expert_dtype="fp8"` (Flash-Base): FP8 e4m3 + float32 block (128, 128) scales, which needs no Blackwell hardware. candidates.title: [Bug] DeepSeek V4.1: natural EOS with unclosed reasoning produces a successful empty answer
candidates.snippet: ### Describe the bug  A DeepSeek-V4.1 thinking generation can hit EOS without emitting `</think>`. With the current default `deepseek-recipe` output adapter, a reasoning-only generation then finishes successfully with empty answer content and no tool calls. An agent client can interpret this as a completed turn despite having received neither an answer nor an action. candidates.title: [RFC] scheduler: UniBoost, a starvation-bounded schedule policy (#48076-#48079)
candidates.snippet: ## Motivation  Under overload, the existing policies trade fairness for work differently, and none gives a wait bound. `fcfs` bounds waits but ignores work; `lpm` and `shortest-prefill-first` favor cheap requests and can starve large ones; `hrrn` ages by waited tokens. On agentic workloads (long shared contexts, heavy-tailed outputs) we see a long TTFT tail of requests that wait minutes.  UniBoost (*Beyond Prediction: Tail-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference*, ICML 2026, https://yl3469.github.io/
